Wine Lover didn’t have a name at first. It chased sparrows in the wild, rolled in the mud, and wandered aimlessly, sometimes full, sometimes starving.
Until it met a woman dressed in red, who occasionally left it meaty bones or half-eaten fish and rice by the roadside.
She always came in a hurry and left just as swiftly, her scent a mix of pear blossoms and wine—a trail that reliably led to her offerings.
But later, the woman stopped coming. Wine Lover resumed its wandering, though this time was different. It grew especially fond of the smell of wine—the scent of home. It traveled and played until exhausted, then curled up in any nearby wine jar for a drink. A few licks were enough to get it thoroughly drunk, and in its daze, it stumbled onto a wine cart, riding tipsily from Qinghe to Kaifeng.
Drenched in the aroma of wine upon arrival, it became the talk of the village. The villagers spread the tale of the "wine-loving monster dog" that leaped from the cart. Wagging its tail joyfully, Wine Lover inhaled the familiar fragrance, as if reliving the days with that woman. It loved this place—where every whiff of wine felt like home.
